title: Dow Futures Climb on Inflation Data; Micron Leads Gains – Investor’s Business Daily
body:
Wall Street opened higher on Thursday as investors digested fresh inflation data and a rally in technology‑heavy futures, while Treasury yields continued their upward march. The Dow Jones Industrial Average futures climbed roughly 0.6 % after the latest Consumer Price Index report showed a modest slowdown in price gains, stoking hopes that the Federal Reserve may ease its tightening cycle sooner than expected. At the same time, the energy‑sector bellwether Bloom Energy surged more than 12 % after announcing a strategic partnership that could expand its fuel‑cell deployments, and semiconductor giant Micron Technology is under the spotlight ahead of its earnings report later this week.

The CPI release showed year‑over‑year inflation at 3.3 %, a slight dip from the 3.4 % recorded in the previous month, and the core index—excluding food and energy—rose 4.6 % on an annual basis, down from 4.7 %. While the headline figure still sits above the Fed’s 2 % target, the deceleration was enough to lift sentiment across risk assets. Fixed‑income markets responded with a modest rise in the 10‑year Treasury yield, which now hovers near 4.55 %, reflecting investors’ expectation that the central bank may pause its rate hikes after the upcoming policy meeting. The modest yield climb also underscores the market’s view that higher rates are now priced in, leaving room for equities to rally on the back of improving macro fundamentals.

Bloom Energy’s breakout performance was the day’s standout move. The company disclosed a multi‑year agreement with a major utility to install its solid‑oxide fuel cells at several renewable‑energy‑rich sites, a deal that could generate upwards of $200 million in annual revenue once fully operational. The announcement sent the stock up more than 12 % in pre‑market trading, reviving investor optimism about the firm’s long‑term growth trajectory after a period of volatility. Analysts note that the partnership not only validates Bloom’s technology but also positions it to benefit from the broader push toward clean‑energy infrastructure, especially as policymakers in the United States and Europe accelerate funding for decarbonization projects.

In contrast, the semiconductor sector remains on edge as Micron Technology prepares to report its quarterly earnings on Friday. The memory‑chip maker is expected to post revenue in the $7.5‑$8.0 billion range, with analysts closely watching its pricing power amid lingering inventory concerns and a competitive landscape dominated by rivals such as Samsung and SK Hynix. Micron’s performance will be a bellwether for the broader chip market, which has been navigating a delicate balance between strong demand for data‑center memory and a slowdown in consumer electronics. A miss on earnings or guidance could weigh on the Nasdaq‑linked futures, while a beat would reinforce the narrative that the sector is resilient despite macro headwinds.

Beyond the headline numbers, the broader market is grappling with the interplay between rising yields and equity valuations. Higher Treasury rates typically increase the cost of capital, pressuring high‑growth stocks that rely on cheap financing. However, the modest pace of the yield rise—coupled with the inflation data’s slight improvement—has so far allowed equities to maintain momentum. Investors are also factoring in the Fed’s upcoming policy decision; if the central bank signals a pause or a slower pace of hikes, the risk premium on stocks could shrink further, fueling another leg of the rally.

Looking ahead, the market’s direction will hinge on several key catalysts. The Federal Reserve’s policy statement later this week will either cement the view that inflation is on a downward trajectory or reignite concerns about persistent price pressures. Micron’s earnings will provide a clearer picture of the health of the memory market and could set the tone for the technology sector. Meanwhile, Bloom Energy’s partnership could be the first of several clean‑energy deals that might spur a broader re‑rating of renewable‑technology stocks. As these events unfold, investors will be watching closely to see whether the current optimism translates into sustained gains or if underlying macro‑economic challenges reassert pressure on the markets.
